title: Customer-facing security brief: privileges & audit logs
content:
Purpose and audience:
This brief is intended for security reviewers at customer organizations who are completing vendor security questionnaires or evaluating Redwood's controls around user privileges and auditability. The goal is to give a concise, technically accurate explanation of how privileges are modeled under RBAC v2, how audit events are structured and exported, and where customers can obtain supporting evidence (automated exports, screenshots, sample logs).

TL;DR (one paragraph for reviewers):
Redwood v2 RBAC enforces least-privilege through role templates and resource-scoped bindings; all administrative and data-plane actions are logged with a consistent JSON audit schema (timestamp, actor, action, resource, request_id, outcome, metadata). Audit exports can be automated to customer SIEMs via (1) secure S3 delivery, (2) Splunk HEC, (3) Syslog over TLS, or (4) direct API pull. Evidence artifacts (policy YAML, role-binding snapshots, sample audit bundle) are available via the evidence automation pipeline and can be attached to questionnaires or shared during SOC/third-party assessments.

1) Quick RBAC v2 summary (customer-facing):
- Conceptual model: roles (collections of permissions), resources (models, deployments, routes, billing), and bindings (principals -> roles scoped to resources).
- Role types: predefined system roles (admin, observer, infra-operator), workload roles (model-invoker, embedding-reader), and customer-custom roles.
- Scoping: bindings can be global, org-level, project-level, or resource-level. This enables narrow privileges such as "invocations limited to model v1 in project X".
- Approval and change control: role templates are managed through the Console UI and audited. Changes emit audit events with before/after snapshots.
- Delegation: service accounts are first-class principals; short-lived keys are supported to reduce standing credentials.

2) Audit log schema (concise reference for reviewers):
- Core fields (every event):
  - timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC
  - level: INFO / WARN / ERROR
  - request_id: UUID (correlates across services)
  - actor: {type: user|service, id: email or service-id, auth_method: oauth|api_key|mTLS}
  - action: canonical verb (e.g., model.invoke, role.bind, config.update, secret.accessed).
